(sec-changelog)=
# Changelog

Every **resolved issue** of Exudyn, newest first, with the version it produced. The micro version *is* the count of closed issues, so each line below is one version number: 1.10.160 is the 160th issue closed in release 1.10. An issue that was closed without being resolved is in no list: it changed nothing - which is why a release can span more version numbers than it has lines here.

Every entry carries the **type** of the issue, then its **priority** and its **effort** as badges (`LOW EFF` is within 2 hours, `MEDIUM EFF` is within 16 hours, `HIGH EFF` is within 40 hours, `HUGE EFF` is above 40 hours), then who raised it and who resolved it - both omitted when that was Johannes Gerstmayr (JG).

This file is generated; it is written by the tracker whenever an issue closes.

**Only the current release is below.** The issues resolved before it, in the same form, are in the {ref}`issue tracker <sec-issuetracker>` of the documentation, which also lists the open issues and the known bugs; the table that follows is the whole history at a glance.

## Version 1.13 - Newborn (current)

- **1.13.303** `EXTENSION` `HIGH` `MEDIUM EFF` `resolved by: Claude-JG` parallel / multithreaded (#1203)
  - description: C++: add multithreading for JacobianODE2 (analytic jacobians)
  - **notes:** The analytic and automatic Jacobians of the ODE2 equations of objects without Python user functions are computed in parallel when the solver runs with several threads (parallel.numberOfThreads) and the system has at least parallel.multithreadedLowerLimitJacobians such objects; the numerically differentiated objects and those with Python functions follow serially. An ANCF cable of 2000 elements: 20.9 ms per Jacobian serially, 4.6 ms with 8 threads.
  - date resolved: **2026-11-01 20:09**, date raised: 2022-07-12
- **1.13.302** `CHANGE` `NORMAL` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Split CSystem.cpp into CSystemAssemble.cpp, CSystem.cpp and CSystemJacobians.cpp (#3202)
  - description: CSystem.cpp has about 4100 lines: the assembly and its checks (Assemble, CheckSystemIntegrity, the coordinates, the local-to-global lists, the item lists, the Lie group lists), the mass matrix, the residuals, loads, algebraic equations, reaction forces and the post-Newton step, and the Jacobians. Split it by moving functions unchanged: CSystemAssemble.cpp for the assembly and the pre-checks, CSystem.cpp for the mass matrix, the residuals and what belongs to them, CSystemJacobians.cpp for the Jacobians and their derivative terms; the vcxproj and sources.json updated. Decided: before the revision of the Jacobians (\#3201), so that it works on a file of its own.
  - **notes:** CSystem.cpp is split into CSystemAssemble.cpp (the assembly and its checks), CSystem.cpp (mass matrix, residuals, loads, algebraic equations, reaction forces) and CSystemJacobians.cpp (the Jacobians), the functions moved unchanged.
  - date resolved: **2026-11-01 18:04**, date raised: 2026-11-01
- **1.13.300** `IMPROVEMENT` `NORMAL` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` One kind per Create function of UserItemCreator, the variants fixed at recording; exudyn.symbolics.utilities.IfThenElse decided by the type of the condition (#3203)
  - description: UserItemCreator has two kinds and two user functions for CreateSphereSphereContact (without and with an impact model) and for CreateRigidBodySpringDamper (the Tait-Bryan and the intrinsic formulation). The contact needs one user function for all impact models: with the impact factor 0 of model 0 its restitution term vanishes exactly. The formulation of the rigid-body spring-damper changes the structure of the computation, so it stays a Python constant of the recording: one kind with one user function per formulation, and Record makes one recording per kind and variant. exudyn.symbolics.utilities.IfThenElse(condition, ifTrue, ifFalse) replaces the private helper of the user items: exudyn.symbolic.IfThenElse for a symbolic condition, a Python if for a number or a bool, so that code written once for numbers and recordings records only the active branch of a condition known at recording.
  - **notes:** UserItemCreator has one kind per Create function: the contacts with and without an impact model are the kind sphereSphereContact, both formulations of CreateRigidBodySpringDamper the kind rigidBodySpringDamper; the impact model and the formulation are Python constants of the recording, and Record records once per kind and variant. exudyn.symbolics.utilities.IfThenElse(condition, ifTrue, ifFalse) is exudyn.symbolic.IfThenElse for a symbolic condition and a Python if for a number, so that a condition known at the recording records only its branch.
  - date resolved: **2026-11-01 15:59**, date raised: 2026-11-01
- **1.13.298** `EXTENSION` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Symbolic: sparse matrices declared by their triplets, their products on the scalar operations of the entries (#3199)
  - description: revision2026c step RG12.65.7 (\#3168): exudyn.symbolics.utilities.SparseMatrix(rows, columns, triplets) and FromMatrix, A @ v, A.T, s A, A + B, A\[i, j\], ToDense, Triplets: the products are the scalar operations of the nonzero entries, each row summed in the order of the columns as the dense product, so that the results and derivatives equal the dense ones to the bit; measured against the dense esym.Matrix product for band matrices of 20 and 100 rows. Decided: first in Python on the table as it is; the slot kind of the table of the proposal only if a model needs more.
  - **notes:** exudyn.symbolics.utilities.SparseMatrix declares a matrix of few nonzero entries by its triplets; its products are the scalar operations of the entries, equal to the dense product, at 100 rows 3 times faster to evaluate and 5 times faster to differentiate.
  - date resolved: **2026-11-01 14:46**, date raised: 2026-11-01
- **1.13.297** `EXTENSION` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` SymbolicSystem: data coordinates - the data of the items, their postNewton steps and the solvers (#3158)
  - description: Data coordinates are needed in the future (SymbolicSystem refuses them now; SystemVariables leaves them out). The data coordinates of NodeGenericData in the recordings (ObjectConnectorUser has them, \#3102), their postNewtonStepUserFunction recorded, the PostNewton step of the explicit and generalized-alpha solvers of symbolicSystem.py as Exudyn does it (discontinuous iteration, recommended step size), data in SystemVariables and in Equations (as fixed values per step), checked against SolveDynamic on a contact or friction model.
  - **notes:** SymbolicSystem takes data coordinates: the recordable post-Newton functions of ObjectConnectorUser and ObjectGenericDAE update them, and the Python solvers repeat a step while the error of a switch is above the tolerance, as Exudyn's solvers.
  - date resolved: **2026-11-01 14:41**, date raised: 2026-10-29
- **1.13.296** `IMPROVEMENT` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Symbolic: the program of a recording built without the export structure; the code in the node measured (#3198)
  - description: revision2026c step RG12.65.4 (\#3153): measured on a recording of 150000 operations - recording 157 ms, esym.Function 351 ms, of which 287 ms the py::dict entries of GetFlatProgramData that it built only to find the named variables, the program itself about 60 ms; esym.Function finds them by a traversal of the nodes. The operation code stored in the node at its construction instead of the lookup by name in Build would save a part of the 60 ms of a one-off build. Decided: as revision2026c step RG12.65.4, option A, the code in the node at most.
  - **notes:** esym.Function is up to 5.6 times faster to create: it finds the named variables of the result by a traversal of the nodes, without the entries of GetFlatProgramData; measured, the program of a recording is built in less time than the recording.
  - date resolved: **2026-11-01 14:34**, date raised: 2026-11-01

  - description: An object on ODE2 nodes, ODE1 nodes and algebraic coordinates of its own, with the linear equations M q\_tt + D q\_t + K q + E y + C\_q^T lambda = f, y\_t + C\_y^T lambda = A y + B q + B\_t q\_t + g, C\_q q + C\_y y = c0, and user functions for the mass matrix, the ODE2 forces, the ODE1 right-hand side and the constraints, each with the arguments (mbs, t, itemNumber, q, q\_t, y, ..., parameters) of the existing user items, parameters a vector of the item as in ObjectUserBody; the Jacobians by a jacobianUserFunction or the one-pass derivative of a symbolic recording, never by numerical differences (\#3101). Exudyn's implicit solver needs the coupling blocks between ODE2 and ODE1, the explicit solver both kinds in every stage and algebraic equations only where they can be eliminated. The general form of SymbolicSystemBase; the generic object of \#1104.
  - **notes:** ObjectGenericDAE couples ODE2, ODE1 and algebraic coordinates on the coordinates of its nodes: the linear terms by matrices, the nonlinear ones by forceUserFunction, rhsUserFunction, massMatrixUserFunction, constraintUserFunction and jacobianUserFunction; recorded user functions give their Jacobians in one pass; SymbolicSystem takes the object.

- **1.13.276** `IMPROVEMENT` `HIGH EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` exudyn.symbolic: the vector and matrix operations as codes of the table of operations, evaluated in the memory of the program instead of by the nodes of the expression graph (#3176)
  - description: Revision2026c step RG12.65.8 of \#3153. SymbolicProgram computes the scalar operations by their codes, but every vector and matrix operation (sums, products with scalars, matrix-vector and matrix-matrix products, transposes, components, dot product, norm, vectors and matrices of components) by a virtual call of its node class of the expression graph (Symbolic.h, SymbolicVector.h, SymbolicMatrix.h), whose result lies in a buffer of that node. These operations get codes and cases of the table that read and write the memory of the program - one contiguous array of the values of all slots, with an offset and a size per slot -, so that the nodes only record and the program alone evaluates: a recording can then be evaluated by several threads at once, copied to the GPU and exported without the nodes; leaves and item outputs stay nodes. The rules of their derivatives are in the table already. Results equal to the bit.
  - **notes:** exudyn.symbolic: the operations of vectors and matrices (+, -, \*, @, the transposed product, multiply, T, the vectors and matrices of components, the dot product, NormL2, the components, == and != of vectors) are computed by the table of operations in one array of the program, as the scalar operations, with the same results to the bit; a recording keeps no values in its nodes; GetStatistics counts them as tableOperations.
  - date resolved: **2026-10-31 22:34**, date raised: 2026-10-31

A VariableSet becomes the scope of named variables - scalars, vectors and matrices, a name unique in its set -, a recording declares its inputs as a set, esym.Function(expressions, inputs), evaluated, differentiated and exported as a UserFunction; CreateSymbolicUserFunction builds the set of the item signature. Needed by the parameters as variables and the system variables (section 12.7).
  - **notes:** exudyn.symbolic.Function(result, inputs, name) records an expression in declared inputs - a list of named variables or a VariableSet - as a UserFunction without item and mbs; VariableSet holds named Reals, Vectors and Matrices in the order they were added and is the scope of their names; SymbolicSystem composes its system by it.

- **1.13.241** <span class="textred">`BUG`</span> `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Diff of pow is NaN for a base \<= 0 also with a constant exponent, so x\*\*2 of a negative x has no derivative (#3135)
  - description: ExpressionPower::Diff returns NaN whenever the base is \<= 0, also when the exponent does not depend on the variable, where d(a^b) = b a^(b-1) da is defined; x\*\*2 records as pow, so the tree derivative (Real.Diff, Vector.Diff, EvaluateJacobian with flatEvaluation = False) of any square of a negative value is NaN. Found 2026-10-28 by symbolicOnePassJacobianTest.py (\#3116), whose one pass treats a constant exponent apart.
  - **notes:** exudyn.symbolic: Diff of pow with an exponent that does not depend on the variable is b\*a^(b-1)\*da also for a base \<= 0, so that x\*\*2 of a negative x has a derivative; NaN for a base \<= 0 only where the exponent depends on the variable. The same per column in the one-pass Jacobian.
  - date resolved: **2026-10-28 13:32**, date raised: 2026-10-28

  - description: After \#3047 was closed: evaluate the options first - (1) an automatic value of a node of the expression tree used more than once, kept for one evaluation; (2) a more algorithmic form, expressions and statements as in code, which allows iterations but probably not automatic differentiation; (3) intermediate variables stored by hand, traceable; (4) other options. - **1.13.129** `IMPROVEMENT` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` ObjectUserBody: reuse the results of its position and rotation user functions for the same time, coordinates and local position (#3028)
  - description: Measured 2026-10-18 with userRigidBodyTest.py (500 implicit steps, Python user functions counted): per evaluation of the right-hand side, ObjectUserBody calls positionJacobianUserFunction 5 times, positionUserFunction, rotationMatrixUserFunction and rotationJacobianUserFunction 2 times each - the markers, the loads and the connector on it ask for the same values; with the last two results of each function kept, by time, coordinates and local position, 45 % of the calls remain. A change of a parameter or a new Assemble clears the stored results.

- **1.13.126** `EXTENSION` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Sparse matrix results of symbolic user functions with the pattern fixed when they are recorded (#3022)
  - description: Mass matrices and Jacobians of ObjectGenericODE2 and ObjectUserBody can be very sparse. A symbolic result esym.SparseMatrix - triplets (row, column, expression) - or an esym.Matrix built from components, whose components that are the constant 0 are known when it is recorded, evaluates into the triplets of the item's MatrixContainer in sparse mode; CopyOrAddTriplets adds them to the system matrix as for a Python function that returns triplets or a scipy matrix. Revision2026c step RG12.3.7.4.
  - **notes:** A matrix result of a symbolic user function built from components is sparse: its components that are the constant 0 are left out when the function is recorded, and the others are added to the system matrix as triplets; a chain of 300 masses with a diagonal mass matrix and a tridiagonal Jacobian solves in 0.26 s against 3.6 s with Python functions building the dense lists.

  - description: The operator \* of two symbolic vectors is their scalar product, of matrices and of a matrix and a vector the matrix product; numpy multiplies the components. \* of vectors and matrices raises a TypeError that names dot(), @ and multiply(); exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicStarProduct restores the old meaning for the transition. Vector.multiply is the product of the components. Numpy's ufuncs (np.multiply, np.sin, np.sqrt, np.arctan2, np.maximum, a numpy array times or plus a symbolic vector) compute with symbolic operands instead of refusing them. Indexing raises IndexError and takes negative indices, so that a symbolic vector is a sequence; a vector divided by a scalar, 2\*\*x and abs(x) are added. The comparison with numpy in python is a test.
  - **notes:** The operators of exudyn.symbolic mean what they mean for numpy, so that one user function computes with numpy arrays and records with symbolic vectors: \* of two symbolic vectors, of two matrices or of a matrix and a vector raises a TypeError (numpy multiplies the components; use @, dot() or multiply()), as does == of two vectors; exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicStarProduct = True restores the scalar and matrix products for the transition. New: Vector.multiply, numpy's functions with symbolic operands (np.multiply, np.dot, np.sin, np.sqrt, np.arctan2, np.maximum, a numpy array plus or times a symbolic vector), a vector divided by a scalar, 2\*\*x, abs(x), v\[-1\], sum(v); CreateSymbolicUserFunction records q and q\_t of the bodies and systems with their size.   - description: CObject::GetObjectNumber (\#2995) is set by Assemble, so an access function that calls a user function before Assemble (a reference position of ObjectUserBody) gets -1. - **1.13.94** <span class="textred">`BUG`</span> `NORMAL` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Matrix move assignment through a base reference exchanges the memory of a ResizableMatrix or LinkedDataMatrix but not its allocation (#2999)
  - description: revision2026c step RG7.3.4 point 16: MatrixBase::operator=(MatrixBase&&) swaps data, rows and columns; called on a ResizableMatrix through Matrix& (as the access functions take it), allocatedSize keeps the old capacity, so a later resize within it writes past the moved-in buffer - the heap corruption of c3d53a99, reproduced with AddressSanitizer (heap-buffer-overflow); on a LinkedDataMatrix the temporary deletes the linked memory. Fix in the Linalg classes (a virtual move that copies for the derived classes, or no move assignment through the base), not in each caller.
  - **notes:** the assignments of the matrices and vectors keep memory and capacity consistent: the move assignment of Matrix copies when a ResizableMatrix or LinkedDataMatrix is on either side, ResizableMatrix and ResizableVector have copy assignments that keep their own capacity (the generated ones copied the other's), ResizableMatrix a move assignment with its capacity; unit tests under AddressSanitizer (revision2026c step RG7.3.4.1)
  - date resolved: **2026-10-16 00:01**, date raised: 2026-10-15
- **1.13.93** <span class="textred">`BUG`</span> `HIGH` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` ResizableConstVector: setting the same size above 7 again points data to the local buffer of 7 - heap corruption of symbolic vector user functions (#2998)
  - description: revision2026c step RG12.3.2 (found in the pre-analysis of \#2996): ResizableConstVectorBase::SetNumberOfItems sets data = &localData\[0\] whenever the new size is not above maxNumberOfItems, also when the vector lives on the heap; the next write of more than 7 items overflows localData, and the destructor delete\[\]s localData because maxNumberOfItems \> 7. A symbolic user function sets its vector arguments on every call: ObjectGenericODE2.forceUserFunction as symbolic function crashes for 10 coordinates (0xC0000374), works for up to 7; reproduced with AddressSanitizer (stack-buffer-overflow at the second SetAll). Fix: keep data where it is in that branch.
  - **notes:** ResizableConstVector keeps its data where it is while the new size fits, and records the size of its heap memory on every allocation: symbolic vector user functions with more than 7 items no longer corrupt the heap; unit tests under AddressSanitizer, test model symbolicVectorUserFunctionTest.py (revision2026c step RG12.3.2)
  - date resolved: **2026-10-16 00:01**, date raised: 2026-10-15

  - date resolved: **2026-10-15 20:25**, date raised: 2021-01-29
- **1.13.91** `CHANGE` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Eigen without fused multiply-add on arm64, so that the solvers give the bits of x86-64 (#2990)
  - description: revision2026c step RG4.1.3.8: the macOS ARM run of 1.13.75 (tmp/MacOS) fails in six test models, all with LinearSolverType.EigenSparse; the dumps of the Mac agent show identical inputs, a bit-identical explicit solve and a first difference of one ulp in an implicit step. Eigen's NEON packets fuse a\*b+c (vfmaq\_f64 under \_\_ARM\_FEATURE\_FMA) whatever -ffp-contract says; without the macro they multiply and add, as SSE2 does on x86-64. Undefine it around the Eigen includes of LinearSolver.h; to be verified on macOS ARM.
  - **notes:** on arm64 Eigen multiplies and adds instead of fusing: \_\_ARM\_FEATURE\_FMA is undefined around the Eigen includes, and the DenseBase plugin Linalg/EigenPluginNoMadd.h undefines EIGEN\_HAS\_SINGLE\_INSTRUCTION\_MADD, without a change of the vendored Eigen; macOS ARM passes the whole test suite and gives the results of x86-64 (revision2026c step RG4.1.3.8)
  - date resolved: **2026-10-15 13:47**, date raised: 2026-10-12

- **1.13.48** `EXTENSION` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` The portable math functions of Exudyn for Python: initial conditions computed with math.sin or numpy differ per platform (#2956)
  - description: The three models left in UnresolvedOnLinux() after \#2954 compute their initial values in Python with math.sin/math.cos (createSphereQuadContact, createSphereTriangleContact: initial velocities 2\*sin(cnt\*pi/3); generalContactCylinderTest: points on a cylinder and RotationMatrixX, i.e. numpy). glibc and the MSVC UCRT round 2\*sin(4\*pi/3) differently by 1 ULP (-0x1.bb67ae8584ca9p+0 vs ...ca8p+0). With sin/cos replaced by float(exu.symbolic.sin(x)) (EM::Sin), Windows and WSL compute bit-identical ODE2 coordinates in all three models (sha256 equal); the only remaining difference is 1 ULP in np.linalg.norm of the test result (numpy 2.4.6 vs 2.2.4, SIMD summation), while sqrt(math.fsum(x\*x)) agrees. Needed: a documented, vectorized way to call EM::Sin, ... from Python (e.g. a small pybind submodule exudyn.math with sin, cos, ... taking float or numpy arrays), used by rigidBodyUtilities (RotationMatrixX, ...) and by test models; and a platform-independent norm for test results. Changes the Windows references of the affected models (generalContactCylinderTest rel. 4e-5).
  - **notes:** The test models compute their initial values with exudyn.cMath, so that generalContactCylinderTest, createSphereTriangleContact and createSphereQuadContact agree on Windows and Linux to the last bit; UnresolvedOnLinux() is empty (revision2026c steps RG4.1.3.7, RG11.10.7)
